name: Mangue
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Krohn, Haakon S. 2022. Fonología del mangue (chorotega). Káñina, Rev. Artes y Letras, Univ. de Costa Rica 46(3): 7-29. doi:10.15517/rk.v46i3.52228 (open access, UCR portal)
catalog_quote: Todas las lenguas otomangues habladas hoy en día son tonales (Campbell, 2007a, p. 7; Hernández, 2021, p. 1), probablemente como resultado de la existencia de tonos contrastivos en el proto-otomangue. Por esta razón, es muy factible que el mangue también tuviera tonos léxicos, aunque en ninguna de las fuentes aparece información precisa acerca de rasgos suprasegmentales. ... No es posible deducir de la explicación de Albornoz si los contrastes del chiapaneco consistían en cantidad vocálica o en tonos, ya que distintos tonos también tienden a influir en la duración de la vocal. Sin embargo, lo más probable es que se trate de tonos, dada la existencia de contrastes tonales en las demás lenguas otomangues. Por su cercanía genealógica con el chiapaneco y los varios conjuntos de palabras homógrafas que se hallan en las transcripciones, también se puede sostener que el mangue contaba con tonos contrastivos, pero el número exacto y la naturaleza de cada uno son imposibles de determinar. [Conclusiones, p. 25] Por último, se afirma que el mangue presentaba tonos contrastivos.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: All Otomanguean languages spoken today are tonal ..., probably as a result of contrastive tones in Proto-Otomanguean. For this reason it is very plausible that Mangue also had lexical tones, although none of the sources contains precise information about suprasegmental features. [...] Given its close genealogical relationship to Chiapanec and the several sets of homographic words found in the transcriptions, it can also be maintained that Mangue had contrastive tones, but the exact number and the nature of each are impossible to determine.

Both halves of the reported quote are v…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement of stress placement exists or can exist: the language is extinct and the 19th-century transcriptions carry at most sporadic acute marks; the modern phonological analyses (Quirós 1985, 1999/2002; Krohn 2022) state explicitly that nothing can be determined about suprasegmentals, and infer on comparative grounds that Mangue was probably tonal (Quirós: 'tono y cantidad'). Brinton 1886 p. 244 reports only that 'accent' was lexically important (Albornoz's Chiapanec pair nolō 'snake' vs nolô 'flower') and that his sources used only a 'syllabic' acute mark.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Quirós 1999/2002 p. 66 (reconstructed from archive.org FTS fragments): 'Ni la condición de la lengua -extinta- ni la calidad de los materiales consultados permiten aventurar, siquiera, una hipótesis sobre los suprasegmentales. Posiblemente, y porque otras lenguas de la familia los poseen, el mangue tuvo tono y cantidad.' Quirós 1985 p. 93: 'no se puede, por ejemplo, decir nada sobre los suprasegmentales'.
new_statements.domain_note: Corpus language (c. 674 words, 79 sentences from 19th-c. collectors); statements concern recoverability from written wordlists, not observed speech. Krohn cites Brinton by separatum pagination (p. 9) = Proc. APS 23 p. 244.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources treat Mangue and Chorotega as one language (moni1237, ISO mom), known from Nicaraguan (Masaya, Nindirí etc.) wordlists; the only explicit 'accent' minimal pair cited (nolō/nolô) is actually from Albornoz's grammar of the sister language Chiapanec (chia1262), applied to Mangue by analogy. Glottolog's Massola 1958 reference under moni1237 is an unrelated Australian item.

tone_statements.citation: Krohn, Haakon S. 2022. Fonología del mangue (chorotega). Káñina 46(3): 7-29. doi:10.15517/rk.v46i3.52228
tone_statements.quote: Todas las lenguas otomangues habladas hoy en día son tonales (Campbell, 2007a, p. 7; Hernández, 2021, p. 1), probablemente como resultado de la existencia de tonos contrastivos en el proto-otomangue. ... De todos modos, la presencia de suprasegmentales contrastivos en el chiapaneco se constata en la descripción de Albornoz (1870, p. 2), quien resalta explícitamente el contraste entre un «acento largo» y un «acento breve». ... No es posible deducir de la explicación de Albornoz si los contrastes del chiapaneco consistían en cantidad vocálica o en tonos, ya que distintos tonos también tienden a influir en la duración de la vocal. Sin embargo, lo más probable es que se trate de tonos, dada la existencia de contrastes tonales en las demás lenguas otomangues.
tone_statements.translation: All Oto-Manguean languages spoken today are tonal (Campbell 2007a: 7; Hernández 2021: 1), probably as a result of the existence of contrastive tones in Proto-Oto-Manguean. ... In any case, the presence of contrastive suprasegmentals in Chiapanec is attested in Albornoz's description (1870: 2), who explicitly highlights the contrast between a 'long accent' and a 'short accent'. ... It is not possible to deduce from Albornoz's explanation whether the Chiapanec contrasts consisted of vowel quantity or of tones, since different tones also tend to influence vowel duration. However, most probably they were tones, given the existence of tonal contrasts in the other Oto-Manguean languages.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 5 'Suprasegmentales', pp. 24-25; cross-reference in sec. 3 p. 17
tone_statements.summary: Chiapanec had a contrastive suprasegmental (Albornoz's long vs short 'acento'); author judges it most probably lexical tone rather than vowel length, inventory undeterminable.

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1886. Notes on the Mangue; an extinct dialect formerly spoken in Nicaragua. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 23(122): 238-257.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: p. 244 ('Phonetics'): 'Accent is of the utmost importance in both these dialects [Mangue and Chapanec].. Albornoz gives this very example to illustrate the importance of accent, nolō, a snake, nolô, a flower. Unfortunately, none of my authorities employ any accentual mark but the acute, and this appears to be syllabic.' All syllables open. No statement of where accent falls.

tone.quote: 2.4. The phonological system of PCM was reconstructed by Fernandez de Miranda and Weitlaner. The reconstructed system leaves many questions unanswered, especially regarding the accentual system. … accentual: accent of uncertain nature Table 6 Phonological System of Proto Chiapanec-Mangue … 3.7. Three tones have been reconstructed for POM: **: (high), **2 (mid), and **3 (low). The tone reconstruction is based, however, on evidence from only PMn, PPn, A, POP, and PCn since information about the tonal features of PCM and PZn is lacking.
